### Observed differences

- In the later window, A04 appears in about 72 in 100 traces (about 15 in 100 before), with mean occurrences per trace up from about 0.16 to about 0.8, and it occurs much earlier (mean event position about 0.17 versus about 0.53); it now co-occurs with each of A27, A28, A29, A33 and A46 in about 72 in 100 traces, preceding each in about 64–65 in 100. [OCC001, POS001, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011]
- In the later window, about 89 in 100 of A04's outgoing transitions go to A15 (before, its output was spread with no target above about 23 in 100), and about half of the observed A04–A15 pairs are one step apart. [DIR002, LAG001]
- In the later window, A14 hands over to A04 in about 70 in 100 of its outgoing transitions — usually immediately (about 98 in 100 of pairs one step apart) — while direct A14→A15 handovers fell from about 83 to about 29 in 100, and A14-to-A15 pairs now sit typically two steps apart rather than one. [DIR005, LAG005, LAG006]
- In the later window, A19, A20, A25 and A26 each send about 92–97 in 100 of their outgoing transitions to A27 (before, they went mainly to A33 and A29 at roughly 40–55 in 100 each), their order relative to A27 and A28 reversed (A27/A28 first in about 22–28 in 100 co-occurrences before; A19/A20/A25/A26 first in about 22–30 in 100 after), and their mean positions moved earlier (about 0.60 to about 0.34–0.36). [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, REL012, REL014, REL016, REL018, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- In the later window, A28 goes to A29 in about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 49 in 100 before) and A29 goes to A33 in about 99 in 100 (about 47 in 100 before), in both cases typically immediately. [DIR011, DIR012, LAG014, LAG018]
- In the later window, A46's output shifted away from A27 (about 83 in 100 before, about 1 in 100 after) towards A25 (about 29 in 100) and A19, A20 and A26 (about 21 in 100 each), with A46→A26 typically immediate. [DIR013, LAG019, LAG020]
- In the later window, participation fell for A06 (about 22 to 7 in 100 traces), A08 (about 18 to 6) and A10 (about 20 to 6); their later routing profiles rest on only 12–14 outgoing transitions. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR003, DIR004]
- Routing elsewhere was stable; for example, A15 still passes almost all its flow to A16 (about 91 in 100 before, 97 in 100 after). [DIR006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural rerouting with two visible parts. Early in the flow, A04 now sits between A14 and A15: A14 passes to A04 about 70 in 100 times and A04 to A15 about 89 in 100 times, A14-to-A15 pairs moved from one to typically two steps apart, A04's participation rose from about 15 to about 72 in 100 traces, and A04 now precedes the late-block activities A27, A28, A29, A33 and A46 in about 64–65 in 100 of their co-occurrences. In the later section, flow that previously scattered from A19, A20, A25 and A26 directly to A33 or A29, and reached A27 from A46, now runs as one near-deterministic sequence A46 → A19/A20/A25/A26 → A27 → A28 → A29 → A33 with typically immediate handovers. These are direct relational and routing changes — observed order reversals and successor redistributions, not just position shifts — consistent across participation, routing, order, distance and position indicators; every item's difference exceeds about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits, and with about 68 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected for an unchanged process, chance cannot explain the pattern as a whole, while the many agreeing items largely describe these two underlying shifts rather than independent phenomena. [OCC001, DIR002, DIR005, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, LAG001, LAG005, LAG006, LAG014, LAG018, LAG019, REL001, REL002, REL007, REL012, REL014, REL016, REL018, POS001, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that both windows sample the same underlying model with a shifted mix of allowed variants — for instance, an A04-between-A14-and-A15 variant and a sequential-chain variant that already existed but were rare before — so a structural modification remains a possibility supported by the evidence rather than a confirmed fact. The reduced participation of A06, A08 and A10 cannot be interpreted further because their later profiles rest on few observations, and several lag items rest on only 1–2 observations. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR003, DIR004, LAG002, LAG003]
